focus: security and traceability -- holdout hygiene and the docs that describe the start rule

findingDetails.title: The README and the shell-step test still say a bare document read is a start
findingDetails.claim: The README row keeps the sentence that a cat of the command document counts as a start while the same row later states the new lookup rule, and the vitest comment above the shell-step table states the same old rule even though every case there also writes a file.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Ran the read-alone input through startState (started false, shape readOnly) and re-read the README row to confirm both sentences live in the same cell. Checked the shell-step table body to see whether the cat case writes; it does.
findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: The sentence can be read as naming the read events the start rule examines rather than claiming a bare read starts; that reading still misleads, because the same row later says a read with no write is a lookup and the test comment says a reader that opens the document is the same start a read tool records.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to ruled-out if the README sentence is read as a statement about which events the rule inspects rather than about sufficiency.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The README and the vitest file are both pass-six scoped scorer files, and the contradiction is inside the single README row.
